To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

top-level and mid-level managers have a greater perception of organizational preparedness for crisis than employees, no difference was observed in the level of preparedness between organizations based on the size of the city in which they are located, government organizations have a greater perception that they are prepared for crises than for-profit organizations.

top-level managers have a greater perception of crisis preparedeness than middle managers and employees, that government organizations perceive themselves as more prepared to cope with a crisis than do private organizations, and that the larger the organization the greater the perception of organizational crisis preparedness.

1) perceived organizational preparedness is higher in top-level managers than in middle-level managers and employees, 2) perceived preparedness is higher for organizations that employ more than 500 people, 3) perceived preparedness varies based on industry type and is higher for government organizations, and 4) perceived preparedness was not significantly different for organizations based on city size.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the organizational preparedness of public and for-profit organizations for a major crisis or a disaster.
the development of a scale to assess perceived organizational preparedness to cope with a major crisis.
the development of a scale to measure perceptions of preparedness for a major crisis or a disaster, and to assess the extent of perceived preparedness for such an event among managers and employees.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the more an organization is able to identify the potential for a crisis and the more it has developed and implemented plans to cope with a crisis, the more it will be prepared for a crisis.
organizations that have more resources and are more likely to have a higher level in the hierarchy are more prepared than others to cope with a crisis.
organizations in general are not prepared for major crises and that there is a need for organizations to prepare for major crises and disasters.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the results of this study indicate that there is a need for further research to determine the level of preparedness of organizations for coping with a crisis or disaster.
organizations are prepared to cope with a crisis and have a plan in place, but they need to improve their crisis preparedness.
the more an organization has invested in crisis preparedness and crisis management, the more prepared they are perceived to be.
The main takeaway from our work is that
organizations need to have a crisis preparedness plan in place and that it is important for them to communicate their plan to their employees.
organizations need to be more prepared than they think they are, and the more employees that work for an organization the more prepared the organization needs to be.
